summary: As of Monday, September 28, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq enters the week with a constructive AI/technology bid underneath it but a less friendly macro backdrop above it. Friday's Nasdaq Composite rose 0.48% to 27,068.72 and finished the week up 2%, with Microsoft and other AI-linked shares helping the rebound. That resilience matters, but it came even as the 10-year Treasury yield ended Friday around 5.20% after reaching a fresh 19-year high, leaving long-duration technology valuations unusually sensitive to any further rise in rates.

The early-Monday cross-asset signal is more cautious. Oil has rebounded after President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz: by 00:36 GMT Brent was up 1.27% at $105.64 and WTI was up 0.76% at $93.11. Trump nevertheless said he expects further U.S.-Iran talks this week, while Middle East crude exports have been recovering, so the oil shock is not one-way. With no major U.S. macro release before the bell, the immediate Nasdaq question is whether Friday's AI strength can absorb renewed pressure from oil, inflation expectations and Treasury yields. Early U.S. index indications were softer, with S&P 500 futures around 0.36% lower; a sufficiently reliable Nasdaq-100 futures quote was not available by the 06:00 Turkey-time cutoff, so I would not infer a precise Nasdaq opening gap.

events.title: 1. U.S.-Iran/Hormuz developments — all session
events.detail: This is today's most important unscheduled Nasdaq catalyst. Trump's rejection of Iran's peace proposal pushed oil higher again, but he also expects talks to resume this week. A further crude spike would reinforce inflation and Fed-hike fears and could push long yields higher, a difficult combination for growth stocks; credible diplomatic progress or softer oil would remove a major valuation headwind.

events.title: 2. Treasury yields and the 5.2% 10-year area — all session
events.detail: The 10-year yield was around 5.20% Friday after touching a fresh 19-year high, while markets had moved toward pricing another Fed increase. With AI shares still providing index support, the key cross-asset test is whether yields stabilize or extend higher alongside oil. A renewed yield breakout would challenge the durability of Friday's tech-led rebound.

events.title: 3. Dallas Fed Manufacturing Survey — 9:30 ET
events.detail: Monday's scheduled U.S. data calendar is light, making the Dallas Fed survey one of the few fresh growth-and-price signals. It is normally secondary for Nasdaq, but with inflation sensitivity unusually high, a strong prices component or unexpectedly hot activity reading could matter through Treasury yields.

events.title: 4. Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin — 12:30 ET
events.detail: Barkin's remarks matter because investors are reassessing the path of rates after the September Fed hike and the recent surge in yields. Any emphasis on persistent inflation or the need for additional tightening could pressure rate-sensitive technology shares; a more balanced assessment could help yields settle.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the constructive scenario is that Brent's rebound stays contained, the 10-year holds near or below Friday's closing area and Friday's AI/semiconductor leadership remains intact; that would suggest the market can continue looking through the geopolitical risk. The downside scenario is a synchronized rise in crude and Treasury yields, especially if the 10-year decisively pushes beyond the recent highs, because that would revive the inflation/valuation squeeze just as the Nasdaq begins a week containing PCE, payrolls and Micron earnings. With Friday's Nasdaq advance occurring alongside 175 new Nasdaq lows versus 54 new highs, I would also want to see broader participation rather than relying entirely on a handful of AI leaders.
keyTimes: The U.S. cash market opens at 9:30 ET / 16:30 Istanbul. The first scheduled intraday catalyst is the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Survey at 9:30 ET, followed by Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin at 12:30 ET. In practice, oil, the 10-year Treasury yield and any U.S.-Iran/Hormuz headlines can override that calendar at any time. This is informational, not a trading recommendation.
